title: Chapter 6: First frost
licence: Original sample written for this project
text: The first hard frost came two nights later. Before it arrived, Ines called the village to the market square. Tomas stood beside her and described the barrels, the carters and the money Asche had paid him. Sabela, with her arm bound, confirmed what she had seen at the gate. Asche called them liars and said that no merchant could be blamed for the sickness of old trees. Ines then read aloud the letter she had taken from the map chest. Oskar rose from the crowd and said that the letter was true. He admitted that he had given Asche the water map to clear his debt, and he laid his warden's chain on the cart. The villagers who had sold their plots demanded them back. The village elders ruled that every sale made since the fair was void, and they held Asche's wagons until the silver and the deeds had been returned. The water map was found in Asche's strongbox. That night the frost whitened every roof in Halden, but the glass trees in the upper orchard glowed and the fields stayed soft. Four trees remained dark and did not recover. Sabela said that a tree which had tasted salt could only be replaced by grafting from a living branch, and that the graft would take seven years. The elders offered Ines the chain of the head warden. She asked that Oskar be allowed to stay and teach her the rows, because he knew them better than anyone and his wife still needed care. The elders agreed on the condition that he never again held a key. In the spring Ines began the first graft, with Pim beside her reading the tree marks aloud.
